subject.title: [Bug]: iOS app fails to connect over Tailscale CGNAT (100.x.x.x) — wss:// required but WebSocket upgrade silently dropped

question: Should native iOS Tailscale Gateway setup remain secure-only for `.ts.net` and `100.64.0.0/10`, or should OpenClaw add a narrow plaintext Tailnet exception?
rationale: Current source and tests intentionally force TLS for Tailnet hosts, but the reporter's reproduced plain-gateway Tailnet setup cannot satisfy that TLS requirement without Serve/native TLS/trust work.

options.title: Keep secure-only Tailnet
options.body: Keep `.ts.net` and CGNAT plaintext fail-closed, improve Serve/MagicDNS/TLS diagnostics, and document raw Tailnet IPs as unsupported for iOS first-run remote setup.

options.title: Allow narrow plaintext Tailnet
options.body: Permit explicit plaintext for Tailscale CGNAT only after a security review defines trust assumptions, UI warnings, and regression tests.

options.title: Defer to UI-only mitigation
options.body: Treat the remaining work as clearer mobile guidance through the open UI PRs and leave the secure transport behavior unchanged for now.

recommendation.title: Keep secure-only Tailnet
recommendation.body: Keep `.ts.net` and CGNAT plaintext fail-closed, improve Serve/MagicDNS/TLS diagnostics, and document raw Tailnet IPs as unsupported for iOS first-run remote setup.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses setup-code routing, TLS trust, and Tailscale security policy where steipete has recent adjacent history and product/security context.
